_comment: What this template took from the repository it was extracted from, what it declined, and why. skeletor was extracted from one mature production repository and that repository kept going, so 'am I current' has a second meaning here that no gate in this tree can ask. THIS FILE IS THE RECORD, AND IT IS PUBLIC. The operator's half — which repository, where it is, and how far it has been read — lives in `upstream.local.json`, which is gitignored, because it names a private repository and because it is right on one machine and wrong on every other. A fork writes its own; it does not edit this one. Read by bin/skeletor-maintain, never merged from.
_the_split: Two jobs were in one file until 2026-09-08, and the day skeletor went public was the day that stopped working. A decision record generalises and belongs in git — the rulings below are the useful half to anybody reading this repository. A pointer to a private checkout does not generalise, is a disclosure rather than a decision, and belonged to whoever is running the tool. Keeping them together meant a fork could not change the config without diverging from our origin, and meant a public file carried a resolvable pointer into a private tree that nobody had decided to publish. Same class as everything else in this repository's notes: a fact that was safe when written, with the world moving underneath it.

upstreams._comment: Empty on purpose — this is the public record, not the operator's configuration. Declare what you watch in `upstream.local.json`: an object of `{ name: { origin, why, read_through, read_on, sources } }`, plus an optional `search_root` naming the directory whose immediate children are searched (default: the directory holding this checkout). Located by ORIGIN URL, never by a recorded path, because a stale path resolves to *some* directory and reads that one's history instead of failing. Keys beginning with `_` are ignored here and there.

_not_taken._comment: Judged and declined, with the reason, so the next pass does not re-litigate it. An entry here is a decision; delete it if the reason stops holding rather than silently harvesting anyway. Subjects are described rather than named by path: the ruling is what generalises and what stops the work being redone, and the file it was about is in a repository a reader of this one cannot open. Nothing mechanical reads these — bin/skeletor-maintain checks `sources`, not this — so the description costs nothing a path would have bought.

jam.sense.their drainer module, in full: Two and a half thousand lines of uptime monitors, an escalation policy and a run ledger. The template ships ONE fully-worked job on purpose — a registry seeded with keys whose modules do not exist is red on arrival — so the drain side stays the adopter's. The capture side ported; the drain side is named by scripts/lanes.py and left to them.
jam.sense.their test-gap lane: A lane with no producer in this template. A view whose label nothing can create is empty forever, and an empty pane and a drained queue render identically.
jam.sense.the editor fallback on a capture (a bare: Worth having and not yet ported. It needs a body template per lane, which is a second copy of Lane.sections unless it is generated from them.
jam.sense.their agent-fix / agent-fix-excluded par: Labels nothing in this template applies. Same rule as the test-gap lane: a lane needs a producer, and a view whose label nothing can create is empty forever — indistinguishable from a queue you have kept clear.
jam.sense.a gate asserting the pinned virtualenv E: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-08, and the correction is the useful part. This was declined as 'correct and unassertable', which was true of the instrument being used and false of the question: `venvPath` is relative to the config file, so whether it resolves is a fact about the CHECKOUT, which no unit test can hold — red in CI, red in an unprovisioned worktree, neither a defect. But bin/skeletor-verify BUILT the checkout, so it is the one caller entitled to ask, and pyright_pin() now asserts the pin resolves to the interpreter the grid built. The decline had generalised 'the tree cannot assert this' to 'nobody can', which is the unit-of-observation rule read one step too far. The limit stays written into pyrightconfig.json for the adopter, where it is still true.
jam.sense.their generated-markdown re-flow fix: Does not apply. Their bug was a docs generator invoked directly skipping the prettier re-flow that the wrapper applied on the way out, so a no-op run rewrote a thousand lines. This template's scripts/docs/ generators never format, so the direct route and the `docs regen` route emit identical bytes and Invariant 4 (a regeneration that changed nothing produces no diff) holds by construction. Re-check if a formatting step is ever added to one route only.
jam.sense.their fix for run-ledger rows written by: Cannot occur here. Their funnel keyed the ledger on `job.key if job else module`, so two hand-written commands deliberately absent from the registry wrote rows under their module name and three consumers each drew a wrong conclusion from the same row. This template GENERATES every report subcommand from the registry and _run_module does a hard JOBS_BY_KEY lookup, so a non-job has no route into the funnel. Re-check if a hand-written report subcommand is ever added alongside the generated ones — that is the exact precondition.
